content.text:
Base directory for this skill: D:\Repos\angular-jig\.claude\skills\house-style # House frontend conventions These are this repo's conventions, layered on top of the SpartanNG docs (the `spartan` skill). They extend the spartan docs where spartan is silent; they never contradict them. Where spartan already has a rule (semantic colors, `class` is for layout only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, `size-*` for equal dimensions), follow the spartan skill; this file adds only what spartan does not cover. One deliberate exception: spartan's examples put Tailwind utilities in the template's `class` attribute. In this repo they never go there; see "Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet" below. Every other spartan rule stands, including "class is for layout only" on a primitive, which now means the utilities a primitive's BEM class applies must be layout only. ## Markup is BEM, styling lives in the stylesheet A template says what things are; the stylesheet says how they look. Utility classes in markup turn every template into a wall of `flex items-center gap-3 sm:w-48` that a reader has to decode to find the structure, and they let styling decisions spread across every file that renders the element. So: 1. **Template classes are BEM names only.** Every token in a `class` attribute, every `[class.x]` binding, and every string inside a `[class]` binding is `block`, `block__element`, `block--modifier` or `block__element--modifier`, lowercase kebab-case. No Tailwind utility appears in a template. That includes `sr-only`: write `class="roster__label"` and `@apply sr-only` it. 2. **One block per component, named after the component file.** `hero-card.ts` owns `.hero-card`, `.hero-card__name`, `.hero-card--retired`, and nothing else. A template must not use another component's block, and a stylesheet must not define one. `:host` is allowed. 3. **Every component is three files.** `hero-card.ts` with `templateUrl: './hero-card.html'` and `styleUrl: './hero-card.css'`. Never `template:` or `styles:`, however small the component. `ng g component` already produces this shape. 4. **Stylesheets are plain `.css` with every BEM class written out in full.** Not `.scss`: Tailwind v4 does not support running behind Sass. The first line is always `@reference "../../styles.css";` (adjust the `../` count to the file's depth under `src/app`), which lets `@apply` resolve the theme's tokens and variants. Write `.roster__row { ... }`, never `.roster { &__row { ... } }`: that is Sass syntax, and native CSS compiles it to a selector that matches nothing, with only a warning. Nesting is fine for states and breakpoints on the same element: `&:hover`, `&::before`, `&[aria-expanded="true"]`, `@media`. 5. **App stylesheets are layout only.** Every utility in `@apply` and every plain declaration in a stylesheet under `src/app`, and every class rule in `src/styles.css`, must be layout: display, flex and grid arrangement, gap, sizing, margin, position, overflow and text alignment (the full list is under "The layout list" below). Color, typography, border, radius, shadow, ring, opacity, transitions, cursor, custom properties and anything not on the list are appearance, and appearance lives in `libs/ui`. Padding is allowed in one place: the component's block root (`.roster`, `.roster--compact`, or `:host`), for the region's inset, and only when that element is not a primitive. Semantic tokens only, `gap-*` not `space-*`, grid for regions. Moving appearance onto a wrapper element, or removing a primitive's directive to keep its look, does not make it allowed. 6. **No utility classes in TypeScript.** No `cva` variant strings, no `host: { class: '...' }`, no computed class strings. A state that changes appearance is a BEM modifier bound with `[class.block--modifier]`. Never build a class name from data (`roster__row--{{ hero.status }}`): write one modifier per state and bind each with `[class.roster__row--active]`, so every class a template can carry is written out in full. Helm directives and their inputs are not classes and stay in the template: `variant`, `size` and the directive itself are the primitive's API. ```html

No rule picks a color, a font size, a weight or a radius: the title is `hlmH3`, the caption `hlmMuted`, the icon's color its `tone`, the retired state a badge variant. `p-6` sits on `.roster`, the block root, as the region's inset. `roster__search` and `roster__recruit` sit on primitives and apply only width and margin. When no existing variant gives the look you need (an input padded to make room for an icon, a quieter table cell, a rounded panel), add a variant to the primitive itself: edit the owned copy of its component in `libs/ui`, add the variant to its `cva` using semantic tokens only, and select it from the template with the input (``). `libs/ui` is the one place `cva` and utility strings in TypeScript belong; rule 6 applies to `src/app`. One variant serves every screen that needs the look, which is the point: a primitive's appearance is decided in one place, not re-decided at every call site. ### The layout list After any variant prefix (`sm:`, `hover:`, `dark:`) and a `!` marker are removed, these are layout. Anything else is appearance. - Display and box: `block`, `inline`, `inline-block`, `flex`, `inline-flex`, `grid`, `inline-grid`, `contents`, `hidden`, `sr-only`, `not-sr-only`, `box-border`, `box-content`. - Flex and grid: `flex-*`, `grow*`, `shrink*`, `basis-*`, `order-*`, `grid-cols-*`, `grid-rows-*`, `col-*`, `row-*`, `auto-cols-*`, `auto-rows-*`, `grid-flow-*`, `items-*`, `justify-*`, `content-*` (alignment), `self-*`, `place-*`, `gap-*`. - Sizing: `w-*`, `h-*`, `size-*`, `min-w-*`, `min-h-*`, `max-w-*`, `max-h-*`, `aspect-*`. - Margin: `m-*`, `mx-*`, `my-*`, `mt-*`, `mr-*`, `mb-*`, `ml-*`, `ms-*`, `me-*`, and negatives. - Position: `static`, `relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, `sticky`, `inset-*`, `top-*`, `right-*`, `bottom-*`, `left-*`, `start-*`, `end-*`, `z-*`. - Overflow and flow: `overflow-*`, `overscroll-*`, `truncate`, `text-ellipsis`, `text-clip`, `whitespace-*`, `break-*`, `text-left`, `text-center`, `text-right`, `text-start`, `text-end`, `text-justify`, `object-*`, `isolate`, `container`. - Padding: only on the block root. Plain declarations follow the same line: `display`, `flex*`, `grid*`, `gap`, sizing, `margin*`, `position`, `inset*`, `top`/`right`/`bottom`/`left`, `z-index`, `overflow*`, `text-overflow`, `white-space`, `word-break`, `overflow-wrap`, `text-align`, `object-fit`, `object-position`, `isolation`, `order`, `align-*`, `justify-*`, `place-*`. `color: var(--sidebar-primary)` is appearance. ### Where appearance comes from - **A primitive's look:** its `variant`/`size` inputs; when none fits, a new variant on the primitive in `libs/ui` (above). - **Text:** a typography directive from `@spartan-ng/helm/typography`: `hlmH1` to `hlmH4`, `hlmP`, `hlmLead`, `hlmLarge`, `hlmSmall`, `hlmMuted`, `hlmCode`, `hlmBlockquote`, `hlmUl`. `

content.text:
The theme and the application shell are in place, and `ng build` compiles. Lint, the contrast gate and the two unit tests pass. The other house gates (`check:boot`, `check:responsive`, `check:interaction`) were not run, and the wiring gate could not run here.

**What changed**

- **Theme (`src/styles.css`):** the spec palette is mapped onto spartan's tokens in both `:root` and `:root.dark`. The full `--sidebar*` set is kept, and `--sidebar-muted` is added. I also added `info` and `sidebar-muted`, which spartan has no token for.
- **Shell (`src/app/app.ts`, `app.html`, `app.css`):** `hlmSidebarWrapper` with `hlm-sidebar` (brand, six nav items, user footer) and `main[hlmSidebarInset]`. Nav icons are registered with `provideIcons`.
- **Top bar (`src/app/ui/app-topbar/`):** a presentational component with inputs and outputs only. It holds the breadcrumb, search, notifications, theme toggle, account avatar, and the sidebar trigger for mobile.
- **State (`src/app/app.view-model.ts`):** `AppViewModel` is provided by `App`. It holds the theme choice, which defaults to `prefers-color-scheme` until the user picks one, and persists it to localStorage. It toggles `.dark` on `<html>` and builds the breadcrumb from the router URL.
- **Routes (`app.routes.ts`):** dashboard, `roster`, `detail/:id`, missions, threats, recruit, settings, all lazy. `/heroes` redirects to `/roster`, and unknown paths redirect to the dashboard. Missions, threats, recruit and settings are new placeholders. The roster reuses the existing `Heroes` component.
- **Config:** `provideSpartanHlm()` is added to `app.config.ts`, as the spartan utils doc recommends.

**Decisions to review**

- **Action text colour:** the spec gives `#ffffff` as on-primary. On amber `#d8891a` that measures 2.8:1, and the contrast gate fails it. I set the light-theme on-primary (and sidebar-primary-foreground) to the dark `#241a05`, which clears 4.5:1. If you want white kept, the amber needs darkening instead.
- **Breadcrumb:** there is no breadcrumb primitive in `libs/ui`, so it is a plain `nav`/`ol`.
- **Padding:** the shell does not pad the content region. Each screen pads its own block root, to satisfy the house-style rule that padding sits only on block roots.

**Not verified**

- The build's initial bundle is 62.95 kB over its 500 kB budget. It is a warning, not a failure.
- The collapsed desktop sidebar (offcanvas) is translated off-screen, which the responsive gate may flag. I did not check it.
- `npm run check:wiring` fails because `harness/counter/check-wiring.mjs` is not in this checkout.
